tagline: Down off the Blue Ridge toward the fairy stones.
intro: From Adney Gap at the Roanoke County line, Routes 602 and 623 come down through Callaway and Ferrum to the Patrick County line near Fairy Stone State Park. A second strand, Five Mile Mountain Road, leaves the Blue Ridge Parkway near Fivemile Mountain and heads for Rocky Mount.

Ferrum was picked in 1911 for a depot on the Norfolk and Western between Roanoke and Winston-Salem. Two years later Methodist women founded a school there for the young people of the mountain communities, and it grew into Ferrum College.

moments.title: Callaway
moments.text: Piedmont Presbyterian Church, said to be the first Presbyterian church in the county, went up about 1850, its bricks reportedly made on the nearby Callaway farm and laid by Benjamin Deyerle's slaves.

moments.title: Ferrum
moments.text: Ferrum College began in 1913 as the Ferrum Training School and is home to the Blue Ridge Folklife Festival.

moments.title: Fairy Stone State Park
moments.text: Over the Patrick line, the park is named for the cross-shaped staurolite stones common around it, and its lake was built by the Civilian Conservation Corps.
